politics.title: Court Finds That Using Copyrighted Material as AI Training Data Is Not Fair Use
politics.why_it_matters: A US federal appeals court (the Third Circuit) upheld the ruling that copying Westlaw's legal summaries to train an AI was not fair use, the first appeals-court answer to the question every AI company's business rests on.
politics.novice_test: A novice does not know 'fair use' or Thomson Reuters v. Ross; introduce it as: US courts decide whether AI firms may train on other people's writing without paying, and the first appeals court has said no in this case. Companion items: JDSupra 'Third Circuit Affirms Westlaw Headnotes Decision' (cand_13 #127) and Pinsent Masons (cand_13 #333).

politics.title: AI regulation takes focus at Abu Dhabi summit
politics.why_it_matters: Abu Dhabi opened its Ai Everything summit with AI regulation on the agenda, and the UAE said it has trained 80,000 government workers as AI 'super users', the Gulf's answer to the US-China race.
politics.novice_test: A novice does not know the UAE's AI ambitions or the Ai Everything event; introduce it as: the oil-rich UAE is spending to make itself an AI hub and is putting AI into every government office. Companion item: CNBC Africa 'UAE trains 80,000 government workers' (cand_13 #118).

politics.title: INEC To Use Artificial Intelligence To Verify Results In 2027 Elections, Detect Cyberattacks
politics.why_it_matters: Nigeria's election commission says it will use AI to verify results and detect cyberattacks in the 2027 elections of Africa's most populous country.
politics.novice_test: A novice does not know INEC; introduce it as: Nigeria's national election body, running votes for over 200 million people, will let AI help check the count, which raises trust and tampering questions.

politics.title: Morocco Joins US-Led AI Opportunity Partnership Amid Washington-Beijing Tech Rivalry
politics.why_it_matters: Morocco joined the US-led AI Opportunity Partnership, a sign of Washington signing up countries to its side of the AI race against China.
politics.novice_test: A novice does not know the partnership; introduce it as: a US club of countries that get American AI technology and training in return for staying on its side of the US-China split.

politics.title: Council of Europe and Microsoft sign framework cooperation agreement to promote human rights in the age of AI
politics.why_it_matters: The Council of Europe, the continent's human-rights body of 46 states, signed a cooperation agreement with Microsoft on AI and human rights, the first such pact with a big AI company under its AI treaty.
politics.novice_test: A novice does not know the Council of Europe (not the EU); introduce it as: the body behind the European Convention on Human Rights, which wrote the world's first binding AI treaty. Companion item: MLex (candidates_55 #156).

politics.title: Pentagon launches 120-day Project Meridian to study AI robotics biotech
politics.why_it_matters: The Pentagon launched a 120-day study, Project Meridian, on how AI, robotics and biotech change the military, alongside its new four-star AI warfare command already in the pool.
politics.novice_test: A novice does not know Project Meridian; introduce it as: a four-month Pentagon review of how fast to adopt AI weapons and robots. Source is a secondary outlet; the primary source needs to be found and read before use.

robotics.title: Video: Dexterous robot hand learns the delicate art of silk embroidery
robotics.why_it_matters: A robot hand (AGILINK) learned to split a silk thread and stitch Suzhou embroidery, a task that takes human artisans years of fine finger control, on video.
robotics.novice_test: A novice does not know Suzhou embroidery or dexterous hands; introduce it as: a robot hand doing needlework finer than most people can manage. Companion item: TechEBlog (cand_11 #23).

robotics.title: Meet Cory, the humanoid robot working at a Waterloo repair shop
robotics.why_it_matters: A humanoid robot named Cory is working at a repair shop in Waterloo, Canada, one of the first humanoids doing a day job in a small business rather than a factory demo.
robotics.novice_test: A novice does not know humanoid robots are already in small shops; introduce it as: a walking robot employee at a local repair shop, and say what it actually does there. Companion item: Yahoo News Canada (cand_11 #254).

robotics.title: 'Big Friendly Drone' will rain death on wilding pines
robotics.why_it_matters: A New Zealand company's $150,000 AI drone finds and kills invasive wilding pines one by one, a machine doing conservation work people could not do at scale.
robotics.novice_test: A novice does not know wilding pines; introduce it as: a tree that spreads like a weed across New Zealand hills, now hunted by a drone that spots and poisons each one. Companion item: B2B News (cand_11 #78). Reserve: 'Humanoid Robot Demonstrates Tennis at Seoul Event' (조선일보, cand_11 #71).

fun.title: Inside South Korea’s robot park, the humanoid future still has some way to go
fun.why_it_matters: Visitors to South Korea's robot park found the humanoid robots greeting and boxing them were being steered by hidden humans with controllers, an instant laugh and a real point about how far humanoids still are.
fun.novice_test: A novice does not know the robot park or Unitree; introduce it as: a theme park built to show off the robot future, where the robots turned out to be puppets. Companion item: Inshorts (cand_11 #242); read Moneycontrol in full to confirm the human-control detail before use.

fun.title: Trump's SI Rebrand Results in Flurry of .SI Domain Registrations
fun.why_it_matters: After Trump ordered the US government to call AI 'super intelligence', people rushed to register web addresses ending in .si, which is Slovenia's country domain, so a small European country got a windfall from a White House rebrand.
fun.novice_test: A novice does not know what .si is; introduce it as: every country has a two-letter web ending, Slovenia's is .si, and 'SI' is now the White House's new word for AI. Companion item: OfficeChai (cand_05 #140).

fun.title: Jailed Albanian mayor uses AI avatar to make deepfake speech
fun.why_it_matters: A jailed Albanian mayor delivered a speech to his city through an AI avatar of himself, politics by deepfake from a prison cell.
fun.novice_test: A novice does not know the mayor (Tirana's Erion Veliaj, to confirm from the article) or Albanian politics; introduce it as: a mayor who cannot leave jail sent a computer-made copy of himself to speak for him. Works as a politics item too.

other_major.title: Waymo Boosts Private Debt Deal to $5 Billion in Push for Growth
other_major.why_it_matters: Waymo, Google's robotaxi company, raised its first private debt deal to $5 billion to fund global expansion, the first time it borrows at this scale.
other_major.novice_test: A novice does not know Waymo borrows money separately from Google; introduce it as: the driverless-taxi leader is now taking on big loans of its own to expand to new cities and countries.

other_major.title: In Race With U.S., China Struggles to Recruit Foreign A.I. Researchers
other_major.why_it_matters: The New York Times reports China is failing to recruit foreign AI researchers despite its push to catch up with the US, a weakness in the race the pool covers only from the US side.
other_major.novice_test: A novice does not know talent is a battleground; introduce it as: the AI race is also a race for a few thousand top researchers, and China is winning back its own but attracting almost no foreigners. Companion item: Chosunbiz (cand_13 #4).

other_major.title: Child Predators Turn to Open-Source AI to Make Unlimited Illegal Images
other_major.why_it_matters: Bloomberg reports child predators have moved to open-source AI image models that no company can switch off, making illegal images without limit; it sharpens the open-weights debate the pool covers from the business side.
other_major.novice_test: A novice does not know what open-source models are; introduce it as: AI programs anyone can download and run at home, with no company able to block what they make. Sensitive: wording needs care.

other_major.title: Tesla Stock: FSD Approved In Denmark; Elon Musk Says This About AI Chips
other_major.why_it_matters: Investor's Business Daily reports Tesla's Full Self-Driving was approved in Denmark, which, if confirmed from a primary source, is a second EU country approval that strengthens the Reuters EU pressure story already in the pool.
other_major.novice_test: A novice does not know FSD is not legal in most of Europe; introduce it as: Tesla's self-driving software needs each country's or the EU's permission, and Denmark is said to have given it. Verify before use; the headline bundles two stories.

other_major.title: AMBA Stock Rockets 18% On NXP Buyout Talks For Self-Driving Chip Maker
other_major.why_it_matters: Ambarella shares jumped 18% on a report that NXP, a big Dutch car-chip maker, is in talks to buy the self-driving chip designer; a notable deal in the car-AI chip field.
other_major.novice_test: A novice does not know either company; introduce it as: the Dutch firm that makes chips for most cars may buy the small US firm whose chips let cars see. Source is a stock-chat site; find the original report (likely Bloomberg or Reuters) before use.

verdict: No, we did not miss a major politics decision: the day's big government moves (Pentagon dropping Anthropic and the court backing it, Trump ruling out US-China AI joint ventures, the four-star AI command, the Hawley-Murphy bill, California's AI laws, Modi's call, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, the UK health rules) are all in the 20-item policy pool, and the window simply held no new decision from Japan, Russia or Latin America. What is thin is regional reach and law: the Gulf (Abu Dhabi summit), Africa (Nigeria's AI-checked elections, Morocco), continental Europe (Council of Europe-Microsoft pact) and the Third Circuit fair-use ruling are missing, and that last one is the one real miss.
coverage_notes: Checked 364 policy, 293 robotics, 156 fun, 222 voices and 186 chosen-source items against today's 253-item pool, the 4-day pools and the 7-day decks by title and topic. Politics volume in the candidates is dominated by repeats (McDonald's AI pricing, OpenAI EU watermarks, Super Intelligence rename, NYC hearing), all already in yesterday's pools, so the sense of 'no politics' comes from those being filtered as old, not from missing them. Europe: EU copyright consultation (Slaughter and May, Pinsent Masons) and a Greek bill limiting AI in HR (Bankingnews) exist but are second-tier; Bahrain's AI misuse penalty bill (GDN) likewise. Middle East beyond the Gulf summit: only a Gizmodo item on US bases and Iranian drones, not an AI story. Robotics: the pool's 15 items are mostly robotaxi business and funding; machines-doing-things items (embroidery hand, Cory, pine drone, Seoul tennis humanoid, Kawasaki shipbuilding robot) were available and not taken. Waymo running a red light in Orlando (WDW News Today, cand_11 #149, video) is a real fail but alarming rather than funny. Fun: strictly, nothing in the window is a laugh-out-loud chatbot or robot fail of the Alexa 'la la la' kind; the robot park puppets are the funniest, the .si domain rush is the cleverest, the jailed mayor's avatar is absurd but political. The Jensen Huang moonwalk deepfake and the gray-cat robotaxi problem were already in the 6 Oct and 4 Oct pools. All links are Google News redirect links copied exactly from the candidate files; each find still needs its article read in full before any writing.
